body.title: fix(auth): shut down the OAuth callback server gracefully
body.body:
Wait for callback responses before closing connections to avoid
intermittent browser EOF errors. Bound shutdown to one second
and cover active responses, forced closure after cancellation,
and the complete browser response.

Assisted-by: pi:gpt-6.1-sol

body.title: Check for new releases hourly instead of daily
body.body: The update check ran at most once every 24h, which is slow to notice a release. It now asks gitea.com at most once an hour (`updateCheckInterval`). The user-facing notice is still shown at most once a day and the Homebrew grace period is still 24h (new `updateNotifyInterval`). Help text updated.

body.title: enhance!: require --json fields and print null for absent values
body.body:
**Breaking:** `--json` and `--csv` now require a field list, and absent values in JSON output are `null` instead of `""` or a missing key.

Like gh, `--json` without fields fails with a usage error that lists the available fields. gt no longer guesses whether the word after `--json` is a field list or an argument, so adding a field can no longer change how an existing command line is parsed. `--jq` and `--template` still read every field the command declares.

Every declared field is now always present: a field without a value is `null` and an empty list is `[]`. Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC to the second. `gt schema` marks date-time strings, and a test checks that no output type leaves a field out.

body.title: enhance!: use gh's flag names for reviewers, maintainer edits, search and repo edit
body.body:
**Breaking:** removed with no aliases: `gt pr create --reviewer-team` and `--allow-maintainer-edits` (now `--no-maintainer-edit`); `gt pr edit --add-reviewer-team` and `--remove-reviewer-team`; `gt pr review request|cancel-request --team`; `gt search issue|pr --assigned`, `--authored` and `--mentioned` (now `--assignee`, `--mentions` and `--author`); `gt repo edit --actions` (now `--enable-actions`) and `--private` (use `--visibility`); the hidden `--before` of `gt notification` (use `--until`).

Teams are requested in the reviewer flags as `ORG/TEAM`, as in gh, and ORG must own the repository. `gt search` takes `--assignee` and `--mentions` with a user or `@me`; without `--repo` they take only `@me`, because Gitea's instance-wide search filters only by the signed-in user. `--involves` and `--no-assignee` are not added because Gitea's search API has no such filters.

body.title: enhance!: use gh's flag names for gt pr merge
body.body:
**Breaking:** `gt pr merge` renames `--message` to `--body` (`-b`), `--message-file` to `--body-file` (`-F`) and `--title` to `--subject` (`-t`). `-s` is now `--squash` instead of `--method`, and `--merge` and `--rebase` gain `-m` and `-r`. There are no aliases for the old names.

`gt pr merge` now takes the same flags as `gh pr merge`, so scripts and habits carry over. `--method` stays, long-only, for the styles only Gitea has (rebase-merge, fast-forward-only, manually-merged), and cannot be combined with `--merge`, `--squash` or `--rebase`. `--author-email` is not added because Gitea's merge API has no field for it.

body.title: enhance!: keep unknown settings and store tokens under readable keyring names
body.body:
**Breaking:** `gt config set` with an unknown key now succeeds with a warning instead of a usage error, and gt 1.x cannot read tokens that 2.0 has moved to the new keyring name.

gt now handles its settings and tokens like gh. Settings files from a later gt, or with settings this version doesn't know, are read, and gt keeps those settings and the file's version when it rewrites them. `gt config get` prints an unknown preference. `policy.yml` still refuses unknown settings, because ignoring a restriction would lift it.

Keyring tokens are stored under the service `gitea-cli:HOST[/PATH]` and the account name, so they can be found in Keychain Access and similar tools. Tokens stored under the old hashed name are still read and moved the first time gt uses them, and logout removes both.

body.title: fix: work with tokens that cannot read the user
body.body:
A `GITEA_TOKEN` without the `read:user` scope made every command fail, because gt first asked who the token belongs to. Commands that don't need the account, such as `gt repo view`, now work with such a token, and so does the git credential helper (Gitea ignores the username sent with a token password). Commands that need the account still fail: `@me`, `--user`, a repository named without its owner, and commands about your own account.

A 403 for a missing token scope now exits 4 (`authentication`) instead of 1, as gh does when authentication is insufficient. Other permission refusals still exit 1. `gt auth login --help` and `gt help environment` now explain which scopes a token needs.

body.title: fix: fix run watch, polling intervals and missing logs in Actions commands
body.body: `gt run watch` and `gt workflow run --follow` now work on servers that cannot list workflows or jobs, as `gt run view` already does. Polling commands require `--interval` of at least 1s, so `-i 1ms` no longer floods the instance. A finished job whose logs are missing, for example removed by retention, is reported as "logs unavailable" and the other jobs' logs still print; before, the raw 404 could show the server's storage path. The missing-runner hint now covers queued jobs even after other jobs started. `runner view --global` no longer claims a runner belongs to the instance, `project … --account` errors no longer name an empty repository, and `run cancel --force --dry-run` refuses a completed run as the real command does.

body.title: fix: fix dry runs, tag data and validation in repo, tag, team and GPG commands
body.body:
- `repo edit --dry-run` with topic flags failed with an invalid repository and claimed settings were changed.
- `repo delete` and `repo archive` with `--dry-run` were refused for a repository inferred from the clone; the non-interactive hint now names the repository.
- `repo archive` with several repositories archived some before rejecting an invalid argument.
- `repo create --team` checked its owner only after the template requests.
- `repo list --archived=false` was ignored.
- `tag list` and `tag create` JSON always had an empty tagger and verification.
- `tag protect` gave no notice when Gitea left out users or teams that cannot read the repository.
- A case-only rename of the owner team reached Gitea and failed.
- `gpg-key verify` with a numeric ID or an unknown key got an HTTP 500.
- A release asset whose name cannot be a file name stopped `release download` from downloading anything.
